decision: Entity identity (Phase 3): a federal body is its supply vote. A B code keeps one entity_id through renames and portfolio changes while it is printed every year; its P code belongs to the same body, including the years after the B vote ends (the residual development vote). A B vote printed again after a lapse is a NEW entity unless a person links it (decision_status=proposed until then). Renumberings link only with a proof (B.41->B.63 and B.49->B.64, approved before the register). Tanggungan (T.*) and the contingency reserve (P.70) are spending heads, not bodies: entity = the federal government with a charged_head/reserve_head breakdown. entity_type gains 'department' and 'vote' (a vote administered by another body: B.11, B.12 under the Treasury). Budget books do not extend a lineage: they reprint lapsed votes with zeros.
why: readable codes are renumbered and reused (DATA_MODEL 4.5); a rule declared before the money is loaded keeps identity from being decided to fit a result; ID issuance stays a human decision

decision: Money flows (Phase 3): a flow is recorded only where the payer's audited accounts show money moving to a recipient. Where the source pays a class of bodies (the state governments, the local authorities) without splitting it, the recipient is a group entity (entity_type 'group') and geo is _unallocated: it is never divided by state by formula. The recipient of each printed line comes from meta/flow_rule.csv by its code, and the build stops if the printed name no longer matches. First slice: PKKP T.12 grants and assignments to the states, FY2010-2024 except FY2015 (OCR-provisional leaf tier) and FY2009 (no activity tier). Second slice (same day): the grants to governments in supply vote B.11 programme 020000, matched by printed name (their activity codes renumber almost every year; a rule may match at most one activity a year); the flow is the activity's 40000 'Pemberian dan Kenaan Bayaran Tetap' line (a block can also print a services line not paid to the recipient). Recipients paid together (Sabah and Sarawak) or as a class (the Federal Territories' administrations) are group entities; meta/group_member.csv says which places each group covers.
why: placing money by an allocation key would make a map look more complete than the accounts are (DATA_MODEL 13); a rule keyed on code with a name guard catches a renumbering before it misroutes money

decision: Lapsed votes (Phase 3, decided by a person 2026-11-05): B.15, B.26 and B.33 each name two different bodies, one before and one after a lapse; all six stay separate entities (decision_status=confirmed). Where their work went in the lapse years is recorded as LINEAGE, a link between two bodies, never one ID: meta/entity_lineage.csv says that named work printed under one body's vote is printed under another's from first_year, and meta/entity_lineage_evidence.csv names the printed programme or activity on each side, re-found in PKKP L1 on every build (E9). Both votes' actual spending tests the move year (E9): the old vote spends on moved work in first_year only when the move is declared moved_mid_year=yes (that year's spending is split between both votes), and the new vote spent nothing on it the year before, unless that spending is the other half of a split the year before (work returning, as MARA to B.22 in 2019). Evidence is the printed activity or programme; only where a volume's activity names are OCR-provisional (FY2015) may the new vote's side be the vote itself (level=vote). Every reused B code is reachable through lineage (E10). Links are recorded at the lapses and the moves that led to them (also Higher Education's gaps under one entity, B.49/B.64), not every move between ministries.
why: in each gap the work was paid from another vote (B.06 for economic planning from mid-2020 to 2022, B.25 for cooperatives and B.22 for MARA from 2009, B.23 for water and environment in 2023), so joining a code's two bodies would make a series with holes and a hidden change of scope; the work divided on the way: B.15's first body sent RISDA and MARA to B.22 and planning to B.06, and the water and environment work of B.33's first body went to B.23, of which only water (with energy) moved on to the new B.33 while environment stayed, so joining either code's two bodies would put another body's work into its history

decision: Placing federal spending by state (Phase 3): money is placed in a state only where the federal accounts name the place. A PKKP development project (leaf row, actual spending) is placed when its printed name names exactly one state or Federal Territory (stated_state) or no state but districts of one state (parsed_district, DOSM 2020 districts, whole words, common-word district names excluded), or a town, region or island listed with its proof in meta/place_gazetteer.csv (parsed_place; added after the blind verifier, with the exclusion of 'di luar Kuala Lumpur'); a name naming several places (multiple_states), only the Peninsula (peninsula) or none stays _unallocated with its total shown. Grants to a named state government or territory administration (fact_money_flow, stated) are placed; class grants are never split (D27). An agency's seat and any allocation key (population, staff, need) are not used. gap_federal_placement reports per state and year the placed amounts and the year's placed_share (placed RM / federal total spending, as gap_need_vs_money's denominator); amounts by state are withheld below 60% (DATA_MODEL 10). FY2015 is excluded (OCR-provisional project rows).
why: a map must not look more complete than the accounts (DATA_MODEL 13); a place named in a project's title is the nearest the federal accounts come to saying where money lands; the method was committed before any result by state was computed
where: core/pipeline/build_federal_placement.py; core/fact_placement.csv; core/gap_federal_placement.csv; meta/caveat.csv CV27; get_gap_view

decision: A class grant is split by state only where the PAYER publishes the split: MOF's Lampiran E (Budget books 2021-2026, actual grants paid to each state, FY2019-2024) is used for a grant and year only where its national total equals PKKP's audited line within RM2 (sources/anggaran/data/_validation_lampiran_e.csv L5/L7). It places those grants by state in gap_federal_placement (method grant_split_by_payer; grants already placed by name are not placed twice; the B.12 grants, paid out of the State Reserve Fund trust account, and grants PKKP does not print as a line are not placed) and gives gap_federal_vs_state a per-state federal side for the capitation and Concurrent List grants (agree within RM10,000, else differ). Lampiran E is not loaded as flows: fact_money_flow keeps the audited class flow; the split is a second source for the same money, never added to it.
why: D27 forbids splitting a class flow by formula, because a formula is ours; the payer's own record of what each state received is a source, and its reconciliation to the audited total is the guard against using a split that does not add up; declared before any result from it was computed
